title: FFT
comment: Comparators (equals32, not ALUs): EOL = (sp == N); EML = (k == N), k through the bypass MUX I125; EIL = (ei == next j). In ML_2, ei is ALU1 directly (mux_com_inner_loop_eil) and next j is ALU2 directly (mux_com_inner_loop_addr2). In IL_2, ei comes from the register and next j from ALU2.

rt: ALU1 -> D -> ei  only so that ei is not 0

states.comment: EOL compares the old sp (before the shift). domega comes combinationally from the ROM delta_omega(sp), so there is nothing to do here for it.

rt: ALU1 -> D -> k  only directly after ML_2 (delay flag)
states.comment: P1 of the group's first butterfly. ALU1 computes ei = k + h, ALU2 computes the next j = k + 1. Directly after ML_2, k is the bypassed ALU1 output (MUX I125). So ALU1, ALU2 and EML already see the new k in the same cycle it is written.
P2: addr2 = j = k, ALU2 computes addr1 = k + h. ALU1 computes the next k = k + sp, which is written one cycle later. EIL here means h == 1, i.e. one butterfly per group.

rt: ALU1 -> D -> k  only directly after ML_2 (delay flag)
states.comment: P1: ALU2 computes the next j = jplus1 + 1.
P2: addr2 = j = old jplus1, ALU2 computes addr1 = j + h. EIL compares the next j (ALU2 output) with ei.
